details: Escalating attacks targeting Saudi energy infrastructure and shipping routes in the Strait of Hormuz have significantly driven up crude oil prices. Brent crude surpassed $110 a barrel for the first time since May, while West Texas Intermediate (WTI) also rose above $100. These developments are fueled by concerns over tightening global supply and intensified Iranian actions in response to US sanctions. The increased volatility and potential for sustained higher energy costs contribute to global economic uncertainty.
title: Middle East Tensions Drive Oil Price Surge Amid Supply Fears

details: The ongoing conflict between Ukraine and Russia continues to exert economic pressure, with renewed attacks on energy sites and significant economic costs for Ukraine. Ukraine's economy is projected to see weakened growth due to the prolonged invasion, labor shortages, and high energy costs. Concerns also persist regarding Russia's ability to supply diesel to the global market, further contributing to energy market instability.
sourceName: Centre for Economic Strategy (via World Bank for economic projections)
title: Ukraine-Russia Conflict Continues with Economic and Energy Impacts

details: China and Japan have significantly reduced their holdings of US Treasuries to an 18-year low in August 2026. This move comes amidst rising geopolitical tensions and growing concerns over the US's fiscal outlook, including a nearly $2 trillion budget deficit in the 2026 fiscal year. While overall foreign holdings of US Treasuries still climbed due to purchases by other countries like Britain and Canada, the actions of China and Japan signal a diversification of foreign exchange reserves and could impact the US dollar's strength and global financial stability.
sourceName: South China Morning Post (via YouTube for direct quote from news)
title: China and Japan Reduce Holdings of US Treasuries Amid Geopolitical Tensions
